title: Total steric changes were smaller than thermal changes in 76% of large local Atlantic thermal changes in NOAA fields for 2005-2025
abstract: We tested annual changes in NOAA upper-700-m thermal and total steric fields for 2005-2025. We selected large local thermal changes using a 90th-percentile threshold that omits the scored start year. In the Atlantic, the total-to-thermal weighted squared-change ratio was 0.523, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of 0.484 to 0.560. The ratio for other changes was 0.880. Total changes were smaller in absolute size in 76.4% of large-change cases. Threshold and latitude checks retained the main result. A post-score linear benchmark gave an observed-to-predicted extreme squared-change ratio of 1.082, with limits of 0.975 to 1.196. Thus the contrast does not establish a nonlinear response. One mapped product, overlapping pairs and uncertainty conditional on fitted residuals, thresholds and linear fits limit inference. This result concerns thermal-selected changes, not total sea-level tail risk. The package includes code, basin/year summaries, source hashes, audits and a figure.

display.caption: Annual total and thermal squared changes and attenuation shares during large local thermal changes. Lines show conditional 95% three-year block intervals.

citations.reason: We read its mean squared-change result and reuse the two NOAA source snapshots. This study adds extreme conditioning and a linear reference test. No code was reused.
